mainTopic: Whether יד (a half-finished statement) works for צדקה, הפקר and setting aside a בית הכסא; then how strict רבי עקיבא is about 'מנודה אני לך'
overview: This amud opens with the last line of a ברייתא, which reads the פסוק about not delaying vows as also covering לקט, שכחה and פאה. The גמרא then asks whether יד, a half-finished statement, works for צדקה. An example is someone who says 'this coin is for צדקה' and then, about a second coin, says only 'and this.' The question depends on how far the link between צדקה and קרבנות goes. The גמרא asks the same question about הפקר. It objects that this is the same as the צדקה question. It answers that the הפקר question is a follow-up: assuming יד works for צדקה, perhaps הפקר is different because it is open to rich people too. רבינא asks the same kind of question about setting aside a room as a בית הכסא. The גמרא explains that he asked one question inside another: first whether זימון works at all, then whether יד works. That question remains unanswered. Finally, on the משנה's case of 'מנודה אני לך', אביי says even רבי עקיבא gives no מלקות. רב פפא then names two wordings that everyone agrees on and asks where the real argument lies, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: 'Of you' includes gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by reading the word 'מעמך' as referring to לקט, שכחה and פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of you' refers to gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא that began before this section. It explains which obligations the פסוק about not delaying vows covers. The word 'מעמך' teaches that the gifts left for the poor are included too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ה׳ will surely require it of you.' The ברייתא reads 'of you' as the gifts that come from your own field for the poor. So the ban on delaying, בל תאחר, applies to these gifts as well, not only to קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of you,' a word from the פסוק about not delaying vows
Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest and are left for the poor
Forgotten sheaves, which are left for the poor
The corner of the field, which is left for the poor

phrases.english: 'Of you,'
phrases.notes: This word comes from דברים 23:22, the פסוק about not delaying what you vowed.

phrases.english: this is gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on delaying vowed obligations also covers לקט, שכחה and פאה.

steps.title: Does a partial expression work for charity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether יד works for צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there יד for charity, or is there no יד for charity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Does a half-finished statement work when someone gives צדקה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נדרים, an incomplete phrase whose meaning is clear (יד) still takes effect. The גמרא wants to know if the same is true for setting money aside for צדקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'hand' or 'handle': an incomplete phrase that still shows what the person means

phrases.english: Is there 'yad' for charity,
phrases.notes: יד means a half-said statement that still counts, the way a handle lets you pick up a whole pot.

phrases.english: or is there no 'yad' for charity?

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ יָד לִצְדָקָה, אוֹ אֵין יָד לִצְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the earlier link between צדקה and vows leads into this question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an incomplete expression take effect for צדקה?

steps.title: Saying 'this one too' is not a partial expression
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. It rejects a case where he said 'this one too,' because that is a full statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he said, 'This coin is for charity, and this one also,' that is charity itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to define the case of the question. It throws out the first suggestion because that wording is not partial at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he said 'and this one also,' the word 'also' clearly ties the second coin to צדקה. That is a complete statement, so there is no question of יד.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
If you say (a suggestion that is about to be rejected)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he said:
'This coin is for charity, and this one also' —
that is charity itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to define the case behind the question in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggested case as the setting of the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With the word 'also' the statement is complete, so it is not יד.

steps.title: The real case: 'and this' without 'also'
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he said 'and this' but left out 'also.' Did he mean צדקה, or general spending money?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said 'this' and did not say 'also.' What is the law? Does he mean 'this is also charity,' or perhaps 'and this' means it is just for general spending, and he did not finish his sentence?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case of the question. It also spells out the two possible ways to read the man's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'also,' his words could mean the second coin is for צדקה too. They could also mean he was starting to say it is for his own spending and stopped. This is exactly a case of an unclear, partial statement.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second reading means he took his gift back. It means his words may never have been a gift at all; he might have been about to say the coin is for himself.

phrases.english: Rather, for example, where he said 'this'
and did not say 'also,' what is the law?
Is he saying, 'this is also charity,'
or perhaps, what does 'and this' mean?
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'also' here, in round brackets; the corrected wording leaves it out and adds 'what', in square brackets.

phrases.english: he is saying it is just for general spending,
and it is his statement that he did not finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in step 3 with the real case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is 'and this' said without 'also,' which can be read two ways.

steps.title: The two sides: is charity like קרבנות for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe יד works for צדקה because צדקה is linked to קרבנות. Or maybe that link only teaches בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: since charity is linked to offerings, as it is written 'with your mouth,' which means charity, then just as offerings have יד, charity also has יד? Or perhaps it is linked only for 'do not delay'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the question. It leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'בפיך' (דברים 23:24) is read as צדקה, and it appears right next to the laws of קרבנות. If the comparison is a full one, יד works for צדקה. If it only teaches בל תאחר, the rule of יד does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared (linked by a פסוק, a היקש)
'With your mouth' (דברים 23:24), read as referring to צדקה
The ban on delaying what you vowed

steps.whatToRemember: The question depends on how wide the comparison between צדקה and קרבנות is: for all their laws, or only for בל תאחר.

phrases.english: Do we say:
since it is compared to offerings,
as it is written: 'with your mouth' — this is charity.
just as offerings have 'yad,'
so too charity has 'yad.'
Or perhaps it is for 'do not delay'
that it is compared?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two readings set up in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the comparison between צדקה and קרבנות cover יד, or only בל תאחר?

steps.title: Does a partial expression work for declaring property ownerless?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there יד for ownerless property, or perhaps there is no יד for ownerless property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a parallel question. Does a half-finished statement work when someone gives up ownership of his property?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same as before, but about הפקר instead of צדקה. The next line will show that these two questions really depend on the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownerless property; declaring something free for anyone to take

phrases.english: Is there 'yad' for ownerless property,
or perhaps there is no 'yad' for ownerless property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as step 2, applied to הפקר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an incomplete expression take effect for הפקר?

steps.title: The ownerless-property question is the same as the charity question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the question about הפקר is the same as the question about צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as charity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the הפקר question is not a separate question. It is the same as the צדקה question already asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says that declaring property הפקר makes it available to the poor, so it seems to work like צדקה. If so, whatever answer we give for צדקה should also apply to הפקר, and there is nothing new to ask. The next step answers this objection.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only an objection. In the next step the גמרא shows that the הפקר question is a separate follow-up question.

phrases.english: That is the same as charity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question of step 6, claiming it is the same as the צדקה question of steps 2 through 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating הפקר as a separate question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הפקר is like צדקה, so the two questions are the same.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate question about יד for הפקר (step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הפקר seems to be just like צדקה, so its answer should follow the צדקה question and asking it separately looks pointless.

steps.title: The הפקר Question Is Built on the צדקה Question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the הפקר question is not the same as the צדקה question. It is asked in the style of 'if you say.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He is asking it in the style of 'if you say.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from step 7, which said the הפקר question is the same as the צדקה question. It sets up the next line, which spells out the new question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said: if we know the answer for צדקה, we know it for הפקר too. The answer is that the הפקר question only starts once we assume יד works for צדקה. It is a second question stacked on the first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say…' (assume one answer and ask a further question)

phrases.english: He is asking it in the style of 'if you say.'
phrases.notes: First assume the answer to the צדקה question, then ask about הפקר.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the question as a follow-up question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הפקר question seemed to be the same as the צדקה question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הפקר question is a separate question that assumes יד works for צדקה.

steps.title: If יד Works for Charity, Does It Work for Ownerless Property?
steps.stepSummary: Assume יד works for צדקה, because a היקש is applied fully. Is הפקר like צדקה, or is it different because הפקר is open to rich people too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say יד works for צדקה, because a comparison is not applied only halfway, then: do we say הפקר is the same as צדקה? Or maybe צדקה is different, because צדקה is only for poor people, while הפקר is for both poor and rich people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the full הפקר question. It assumes יד works for צדקה and asks whether הפקר follows the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the גמרא assumes one answer to the צדקה question, without deciding it: perhaps the link to קרבנות applies fully, since a היקש is not applied halfway. On that assumption, it asks whether הפקר is like צדקה. The possible difference is that צדקה goes only to the poor, while הפקר is open to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: a comparison between two topics based on how the פסוק puts them together

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר יֵשׁ יָד לִצְדָקָה,
phrases.english: If you say a partial statement works for charity,
because a comparison is not applied only halfway,
phrases.notes: This is the link between צדקה and קרבנות from step 5. If it applies, it applies fully, not only for בל תאחר.

phrases.english: do we say ownerless property is the same as charity,
or perhaps charity is different,
because charity is fit only for poor people,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֶפְקֵר בֵּין לַעֲנִיִּים בֵּין לַעֲשִׁירִים?
phrases.english: but ownerless property is for both poor and rich people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the follow-up question announced in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הפקר follows צדקה in allowing יד, or is different because it is open to rich people too.
steps.whatToRemember: The הפקר question stands only if יד works for צדקה. The possible difference is that צדקה is only for the poor, while הפקר is for everyone. The question is left open.

steps.title: רבינא Asks About a Bathroom
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks whether יד works when setting aside a room as a בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked: does a partial statement work for a bathroom, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new question. He asks whether יד works when someone sets aside a building as a בית הכסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the questions were about money and property (צדקה, הפקר). Now the same idea of יד is tested on a different kind of statement: setting aside a place for a certain use.

keyTerms.meaning: asked (a real question he was unsure about)

phrases.english: Ravina asked:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ יָד לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Does a partial statement work for a bathroom, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question using the same idea of יד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יד works when setting aside a place as a בית הכסא.

steps.title: Not When He Said 'This One Too'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. It rejects a case where he said 'this one too,' because that is a full statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he said, 'This house should be a bathroom, and this one too,' then that one is plainly a bathroom too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the exact case is, then rejects the first possible case. This is the same pattern as step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he said 'this one too,' he clearly included the second house, so there is nothing to ask. A real question needs an unclear statement.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he said,
'This house should be a bathroom,
and this one too,'
that one is plainly a bathroom too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case of רבינא's question and rejects one option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case where he said 'this one too.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That statement is complete and clear, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: He Said 'And This' Without 'Also'
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he said 'and this' but left out 'also.' Did he mean a bathroom, or just general use?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he said 'and this,' and did not say 'also.' What did he mean by 'this'? 'And this is also a bathroom'? Or perhaps, by 'and this,' he only meant it is for general use?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case: he said 'and this' without 'also.' It explains the two ways to read his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'also,' it is unclear whether the second house was included in the first statement. If it was, this is יד for a בית הכסא. If not, he only meant the house is for everyday use.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he said 'and this,'
and did not say 'also.'
What did he mean by 'this'?
'And this is also a bathroom,'
or perhaps, what does 'and this' mean?
He is saying it is just for general use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct case after step 11 rejected the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is 'and this' without 'also.' The question is whether he meant a bathroom or only general use.

steps.title: Wasn't רבינא Unsure Whether Setting Aside Works at All?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's question seems to assume that זימון for a בית הכסא works. But elsewhere רבינא was unsure about that very point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean it is obvious to רבינא that setting aside a place as a bathroom works? But רבינא was unsure about this! He asked: if he set it aside as a bathroom, what is the law? If he set it aside as a bathhouse, what is the law? Does setting aside work, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא's question. Asking about יד only makes sense if a full זימון works, but רבינא himself was unsure whether זימון works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking about a partial statement assumes that a full statement works. Yet in another place רבינא asked whether only setting aside a place, before it is actually used, makes it a בית הכסא or a בית המרחץ. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: setting aside a place for a use, before it is used

phrases.english: Does this mean it is obvious to Ravina
that setting aside a place as a bathroom works?
But Ravina was unsure about this:
If he set it aside as a bathroom, what is the law?
If he set it aside as a bathhouse, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: זִימּוּן מוֹעִיל, אוֹ אֵין זִימּוּן מוֹעִיל?
phrases.english: Does setting aside work, or does it not work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבינא's question in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's question about יד for a בית הכסא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking about יד assumes זימון works, but רבינא himself was unsure whether זימון works.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. One asks whether setting aside works at all (זימון). The other asks whether a partial statement of setting aside works (יד).

steps.title: One Question Inside Another
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asked two questions, one built on the other. First: does זימון work? Then: if it does, does יד work too? The question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked one question inside another. First: does setting aside work or not? If you say it works, then: does a partial statement work or not? Let it remain a question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבינא really asked two stacked questions, so there is no contradiction, and the question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question is whether זימון works at all. The second question, about יד, only starts once you assume זימון works. This is the same 'if you say' structure the גמרא used for צדקה and הפקר.
steps.whatToRemember: Both here and with צדקה and הפקר, the גמרא uses stacked questions. You only reach the second question by assuming an answer to the first. Here the questions about זימון and יד for a בית הכסא remain open.
steps.whyThisMatters: Explaining the 'if you say' structure removes both contradictions in this section, and it shows how the גמרא builds questions in layers.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Ravina asked one question inside another:

phrases.aramaic: זִימּוּן מוֹעִיל אוֹ אֵין זִימּוּן מוֹעִיל.
phrases.english: Does setting aside work, or does it not work?
If you say setting aside works:
does a partial statement work, or not?
Let it remain a question.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא חֲדָא מִגּוֹ חֲדָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא's question about יד seemed to assume that זימון works, which contradicts his other question.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא first asked whether זימון works, and only then, assuming it does, asked about יד. The question remains open.

steps.title: אביי: Even רבי עקיבא gives no lashes for this vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of 'מנודה אני לך'. אביי says רבי עקיבא agrees that someone who breaks this kind of vow does not get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the line in the משנה, 'I am ostracized from you, etc.': אביי said that רבי עקיבא agrees that, when it comes to lashes, the person is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. אביי then limits how strict רבי עקיבא really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא only 'leaned toward being strict' about this wording. אביי explains that this leaning tells the person not to break the vow. It does not go so far as to give him מלקות if he does break it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am ostracized from you': a way of cutting oneself off from someone that may work as a vow
agrees (to a point he might seem to argue on)
lashes, the punishment for breaking a real Torah vow

steps.confusionAlert: Being strict is not the same as giving מלקות. רבי עקיבא can forbid the person to benefit and still not punish him with lashes.

phrases.english: 'I am ostracized from you,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The 'etc.' covers the rest of that line, where רבי עקיבא leaned toward being strict.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi Akiva agrees regarding lashes
that he is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנוּדֶּה אֲנִי לָךְ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The question about יד for a בית הכסא was left open in Step 14, and now the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי עקיבא, someone who breaks a 'מנודה אני לך' vow does not get מלקות.

steps.title: Proof from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his point from the משנה's wording. If רבי עקיבא held that the person gets lashes, the משנה would just say 'רבי עקיבא is strict.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For if he really held the person gets lashes, let the משנה simply say: 'רבי עקיבא is strict.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his claim by looking closely at the words the משנה chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say 'רבי עקיבא is strict.' It uses softer words: he 'leaned toward being strict.' That shows he was not fully sure. You do not give lashes when you are unsure, so there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: for if so (if the opposite were true)
let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: For if so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי עקיבא really held that the person gets lashes.

phrases.english: let it teach: 'Rabbi Akiva is strict.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind אביי's ruling in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי עקיבא gives no מלקות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's soft wording ('leaned toward being strict') in place of a plain 'רבי עקיבא is strict'

steps.title: רב פפא: Two wordings everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא marks two clear cases. Saying 'נדינא מינך' makes him forbidden according to everyone. Saying 'משמתנא מינך' leaves him permitted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If he said 'I am distanced from you,' everyone agrees he is forbidden. If he said 'I am excommunicated from you,' everyone agrees he is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets the limits of the argument by naming one wording that clearly works as a vow and one that clearly does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נדינא' is language of distancing oneself, which counts as a partial expression (יד) of a vow, so it forbids him. 'משמתנא' is the language of שמתא, a ban, and not the language of vows, so it does nothing. With both edges fixed, the real argument must sit somewhere in between.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am distanced from you': counts as a vow
'I am excommunicated from you': language of a ban, not a vow

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With 'I am distanced from you,'
everyone agrees that he is forbidden.
'I am excommunicated from you'
according to everyone, he is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בִּ״נְדִינָא מִינָּךְ״ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the same משנה about נידוי-language. Now the focus moves from punishment to which exact words count as a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'נדינא מינך' forbids him according to everyone. 'משמתנא מינך' permits him according to everyone.

steps.title: So where is the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: After naming the two agreed cases, רב פפא asks which wording the argument in the משנה is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: So about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks the question, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once both edges are agreed on, the argument in the משנה must be about some third wording. This question points us to find it.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 17: with both edges agreed, it asks for the case the argument is really about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which exact wording the argument about 'מנודה אני לך' is really about, since 'נדינא' and 'משמתנא' are both agreed on.
